name: WebGL parameters and extensions
plain: Reads the GPU vendor and model string, hardware limits and the list of supported WebGL extensions.
meaning: Exposes the exact GPU model and driver family (for example 'ANGLE (Apple, M2)'), which is a strong device class signal and reveals gaming, laptop or phone hardware.

steps: Create a WebGL context on a hidden canvas
Call getParameter on 60 or more constants

safari.note: Debug renderer returns generic 'Apple GPU' on Apple silicon since about Safari 15

data.metric: About 70 numeric limits plus 30 to 40 extension names

fields.name: UNMASKED_RENDERER_WEBGL
fields.precision: full model on Chrome and Firefox desktop

limits.headline: Can see your graphics card model, limits and which 3D features it supports
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads
can: Get the graphics chip name, for example Apple M2
Get its hardware limits and feature list
Tell if you use a phone, laptop or gaming PC
cannot: Get the real chip name in browsers that mask it
limits.differs: Safari and some Android browsers hide the chip name more than Chrome and Edge on desktop.

story.what_it_is: A script reads your GPU's vendor and model string, hardware limits and the list of supported WebGL extensions.

marketing.name: WebGL extensions
marketing.pitch: Describes optional graphics features a browser may offer on top of the base WebGL set.

story.for_you: You never see it. Your device quietly answers a long list of graphics questions. The answers are nearly the same each visit, so they help a site recognize your device.
story.for_makers: Game and 3D makers read these to pick textures and effects. Fraud teams and trackers read the same list because it separates graphics chips and driver versions.

use_cases.example: A browser game like those running Unity or Babylon in a tab checks supported extensions, then picks the best texture format.
A 3D editor in the browser checks which features exist, then turns on or off shadows and effects.
A web map checks for float textures so it can draw smooth terrain on newer chips.
A fraud tool compares the list to known real devices and spots a virtual machine.
A tracker hashes the long extension list into an ID, since few devices match exactly.
A visitor counting tool counts how many users have older graphics chips so a site knows what to support.
A game studio checks the crash reports by graphics model to fix a driver bug.

technical_bounds: Needs GPU or SwiftShader, headless can reveal 'SwiftShader' or 'llvmpipe'
Brave and Tor return generic values

value.legit_uses: Pick shader quality tiers, report crashes by GPU
value.abuse: Device class ID, VM and bot detection, spoof checks (renderer versus user agent mismatch)

history.change: Cao et al. NDSS 2017 cross-browser fingerprinting via GPU features
